$comment: StudyFlix autonomous curriculum backlog. Generated by the 5-phase pipeline in CLAUDE.md. Expectation text is quoted verbatim from the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum (2022), Grade 6.
subject: Science & Technology

curriculum.name: Ontario Science and Technology, Grades 1-8 (2022)
curriculum.source: Ontario Ministry of Education, Grade 6 Expectations and Key Concepts

overarchingStrand.title: STEM Skills and Connections
expectations: A1. use a scientific research process, a scientific experimentation process, and an engineering design process to conduct investigations, following appropriate health and safety procedures
A2. use coding in investigations and to model concepts, and assess the impact of coding and of emerging technologies on everyday life and in STEM-related fields
A3. demonstrate an understanding of the practical applications of science and technology, and of contributions to science and technology from people with diverse lived experiences

strand.title: Life Systems: Biodiversity
overallExpectations: B1. assess the importance of biodiversity, and describe ways of protecting biodiversity
B2. demonstrate an understanding of biodiversity, its contributions to the stability of natural systems, and its benefits to humans

topics.title: Biodiversity & Classification of Living Things
topics.description: Sort the six kingdoms of life, run a dichotomous key on Ontario species, and watch an invasive species collapse a Great Lakes food web.
learningObjectives: Define biodiversity at three levels: within a species, between species, and across ecosystems.
Classify organisms into the six kingdoms using observable characteristics.
Use a dichotomous key to identify Ontario organisms from paired either/or questions.
Distinguish vertebrates from invertebrates and name the five vertebrate classes.
Explain how an invasive species such as the zebra mussel or sea lamprey destabilises a natural community.
Describe symbiosis (mutualism, commensalism, parasitism) as an interrelationship between species.
Assess how habitat loss and climate change drive species toward endangerment and extinction, and describe protective actions.

interactiveLab.title: Dichotomous Key & Great Lakes Food Web Lab
stations: Six Kingdoms Sorter: drag 12 organisms into the correct kingdom, with live scoring.
Dichotomous Key Explorer: walk a branching either/or tree to identify Ontario species.
Food Web Collapse Simulator: introduce an invasive species and watch population bars react.

canadianContext: Great Lakes zebra mussel and sea lamprey invasions
Species at risk: Blanding's turtle, piping plover, beluga whale
Boreal forest and Carolinian forest biodiversity

exerciseTiers.tier1: Ontario Core: kingdoms, vertebrate classes, invertebrate identification
exerciseTiers.tier2: Enriched Application: food web energy tracing and symbiosis classification
exerciseTiers.tier3: Waterloo CEMC Style: dichotomous key logic and population collapse arithmetic

strand.title: Structures and Mechanisms: Flight
overallExpectations: D1. assess the environmental impacts of flying machines
D2. demonstrate an understanding of the ways in which properties of air can be applied to the principles of flight and flying machines

topics.title: Flight, Aerodynamics & the Four Forces
topics.description: Balance lift, weight, thrust and drag in a live wind tunnel, shape your own aerofoil, and test Bernoulli's principle at Canadian cruising altitudes.
learningObjectives: Name the four forces of flight and describe the pair each one opposes.
Predict whether an aircraft climbs, descends, accelerates or slows from balanced vs. unbalanced forces.
Explain lift using Bernoulli's principle: faster air over the curved upper surface means lower pressure.
Describe the properties of air: it has mass, takes up space, can be compressed, and exerts pressure.
Relate angle of attack to lift, and explain what a stall is.
Compare structural adaptations for flight in birds, bats and insects with aircraft components.
Assess the environmental impact of aviation, including greenhouse gas emissions and noise.

interactiveLab.title: Four Forces Wind Tunnel & Aerofoil Studio
stations: Four Forces Balance: slide thrust and lift, watch the aircraft climb, stall or stall-recover in real time.
Aerofoil Shaper: change camber and angle of attack, see streamlines and the pressure map redraw.
Bird vs. Machine: compare wing adaptations of a Canada goose, a bat and a de Havilland Dash 8.

canadianContext: Avro Arrow and the Canadarm heritage of Canadian aerospace
de Havilland Canada Dash 8 and the Canadair water bomber
Cruising altitude 11 km, cruising speed 850 km/h, air temperature -55 degrees C
Canada goose migration aerodynamics and the V formation

exerciseTiers.tier1: Ontario Core: identify the four forces and the properties of air
exerciseTiers.tier2: Enriched Application: predict motion from unbalanced force pairs in newtons
exerciseTiers.tier3: Waterloo CEMC Style: multi-step lift/drag ratio and fuel-per-passenger reasoning

strand.title: Earth and Space Systems: Space
overallExpectations: E1. assess the impact of space exploration on humans, society, and the environment
E2. demonstrate an understanding of the solar system, the phenomena that result from the movement of different bodies within it, and the technologies used in space exploration

topics.title: Space Exploration & the Solar System
topics.description: Fly a scale orbit simulator, tilt Earth's axis to build the seasons, and weigh yourself on eight worlds to separate mass from weight.
learningObjectives: Identify the components of the solar system and describe their main physical characteristics.
Distinguish mass (kilograms, constant) from weight (newtons, depends on gravity).
Explain how Earth's 23.5 degree axial tilt, not its distance from the Sun, causes the seasons.
Explain how rotation on the axis produces day and night, and revolution produces the year.
Compare comets, asteroids and meteoroids, and describe what makes a meteor and a meteorite.
Describe space technologies including telescopes, spectroscopes, satellites, GPS and the Canadarm.
Assess the benefits and costs of space exploration for society and the environment.

interactiveLab.title: Solar System Orbit Simulator & Gravity Scale
stations: Orbit Simulator: run the eight planets at true relative periods, click any world for its data card.
Axial Tilt & Seasons: drag Earth around its orbit and watch the northern hemisphere sunlight angle change.
Mass vs. Weight Scale: enter your mass in kg and read your weight in newtons on eight worlds.

canadianContext: Canadian Space Agency, the Canadarm2 and Dextre on the International Space Station
Canadian astronauts Chris Hadfield, Roberta Bondar, Jeremy Hansen and the Artemis II mission
Aurora borealis over Yellowknife and the David Dunlap Observatory

exerciseTiers.tier1: Ontario Core: solar system components, rotation vs. revolution, seasons
exerciseTiers.tier2: Enriched Application: mass vs. weight calculations in newtons across worlds
exerciseTiers.tier3: Waterloo CEMC Style: orbital period ratios, light-travel time and scale modelling

strand.title: Matter and Energy: Electrical Phenomena, Energy, and Devices
overallExpectations: C1. evaluate the impact of the use and generation of electrical energy on society and the environment, and suggest ways to use electrical energy responsibly
C2. demonstrate an understanding of the principles of electrical energy and its transformation into and from other forms of energy

topics.title: Electricity & Electrical Devices
topics.description: Wire live series and parallel circuits, test conductors and insulators, and audit an Ontario home's energy bill in kilowatt hours.
learningObjectives: Explain static electricity as a build-up of charge, and describe discharge.
Compare static electricity with current electricity, the continuous flow of charge in a circuit.
Build a complete circuit and identify the source, conductor, load and switch.
Distinguish series circuits from parallel circuits and identify common uses of each.
Classify materials as conductors or insulators from a live conductivity test.
Describe energy transformations in everyday devices (electrical to light, heat, sound, motion).
Compare renewable and non-renewable electricity generation in Ontario and suggest responsible use.

interactiveLab.title: Circuit Builder, Conductivity Bench & Ontario Energy Audit
stations: Circuit Builder: toggle between series and parallel, add cells and bulbs, open a switch and remove a bulb to see what stays lit.
Conductor vs. Insulator Bench: drop 10 materials into the test gap and watch the bulb respond.
Ontario Energy Audit: switch appliances on and off and watch kWh per day and cost in dollars update.

canadianContext: Sir Adam Beck hydroelectric generating station at Niagara Falls
Ontario's generation mix: nuclear, hydroelectricity, wind and natural gas
Winter static shocks on a dry Ontario January day
Household electricity priced in kWh and CAD dollars

exerciseTiers.tier1: Ontario Core: static vs. current, conductors vs. insulators, circuit parts
exerciseTiers.tier2: Enriched Application: predict bulb behaviour when a series or parallel branch breaks
exerciseTiers.tier3: Waterloo CEMC Style: multi-step kWh cost optimisation and circuit logic puzzles
